findings.issue: コップ１杯 is read いっぱい (counter 杯 with 1 geminates and voices to ぱ), not いちばい. いちばい corresponds to 一倍, a different word.
findings.current: こっぷいちばいのみずをください。
findings.suggested: こっぷいっぱいのみずをください。

findings.issue: Numeral １ in コップ１杯 is realized いっ (gemination before 杯), not いち; corpus token readings elsewhere use surface phonetics (cf. とっ).
Counter 杯 after いっ is read ぱい (h→p after sokuon): いっぱい. Reading ばい is wrong in this context (that is the 倍 'times/fold' pattern).
Romaji carries the same wrong reading: ichibai should be ippai (コップ１杯 = koppu ippai).
六階 is standardly read ろっかい (6 geminates before k-row counters: 六回/六階 = ろっかい, taught in all JLPT floor-counter lists), not ろくかい.
findings.current: このえれべーたーわろくかいよりうえにわいけません。
findings.suggested: このえれべーたーわろっかいよりうえにわいけません。

findings.issue: 六 in 六階 is realized ろっ (gemination), not ろく; token readings in this corpus use surface phonetics (かい stays on the 階 token).
Romaji carries the same wrong reading: rokukai should be rokkai (六階 = rokkai).

"faço-em" is ungrammatical and attaches the に gloss to the wrong word: に follows コート, so the corpus's hyphen convention (cf. "Aqui-para vir") requires "casaco-em". Current text misrepresents the structure the lit field is meant to teach.
English drops ここの entirely ("the university students here"); pt and lit_en keep it, so en is the odd one out and loses the locational anchor.
findings.current: The students are for the most part diligent.
findings.suggested: The university students here are for the most part diligent.
